title: Finite-support Weyl cylinder form invariance and weighted square-root products
question: Does the finite Q3 Friedrichs form domain remain invariant under finite-support Weyl multipliers, with explicit two-orientation weighted square-root product bounds?
method: Represent a finite-support Weyl cylinder as the modulus-one multiplier A_t(q)=exp(i sum_j t_j q_j), so the potential and bond parts of either shifted form are unchanged.
Use the product rule and |a+b|^2<=2|a|^2+2|b|^2 to obtain q_K[A_t psi] <= 2 q_K[psi] + ||t||_2^2/chi ||psi||^2 on the common C_c^infinity core.

Pass through the closed positive Friedrichs form from EXP-001131 to define same-orientation products with squared bound 2+||t||_2^2/chi; pay the exact form-order multiplier 21 for cross-orientation products.
Run independent Fraction-only support vectors, bounded-degree volume fixtures and Lean R303 for the squared-gradient and orientation constants.
finding: Primary 32/32, independent 22/22, integrated 14/14, and Lean R303 PASS. Every declared finite-support Weyl multiplier preserves both fixed-finite-graph shifted form domains; same-orientation weighted square-root products have squared bound 2+||t||_2^2/chi, and cross-orientation products have squared bound 21(2+||t||_2^2/chi), uniform in volume for degree at most six.
decision_reason: EXP-001131 supplied closed common forms and the degree-six order. The exact Weyl product rule now closes a bounded cylinder subalgebra at the form level and gives explicit weighted products in both orientations. This is a direct QFT Weyl-algebra interface, but it does not extend automatically to unbounded polynomial observables or modular real-time dynamics.
closed: fixed-support volume uniformity in the bounded-degree class
independent reproduction and Lean R303 cross-check
open: all bounded local observables beyond Weyl multipliers
direct D and delta-D Cauchy estimates

adversarial_review.check: The Weyl multiplier has modulus one, so potential and bond terms are unchanged; only the kinetic product rule is estimated.
The exact squared gradient norm is ||t||_2^2/chi and the factor two comes only from the explicit product-rule inequality.
The weighted products are defined through closed forms and K^{-1/2}; no arbitrary unbounded commutator or polynomial domain identity is promoted.
Same-form and cross-orientation products are separately recorded, with the cross factor 21 inherited from EXP-001131.
For fixed t the constants do not depend on vertex count within degree six, but this is not a thermodynamic dynamics or common-alpha theorem.
The result is a bounded Weyl-cylinder bridge only; modular transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
